_comment: Fungus candidate-B / Cryptolith Rite (2026-10-14). PROVES THE CREATURE-MANA GRANT IS LIVE FROM A NON-CREATURE SOURCE, which is the one thing no existing test covers. Cryptolith Rite is implemented by reusing Brightcap Badger's granted_tap_mana_subtypes [Fungus, Saproling] + granted_tap_mana_color G -- but the Badger is a CREATURE and this is an ENCHANTMENT, so the question is whether LiveManaGrant's battlefield walk admits a non-creature grant source. It does by inspection (SpellEffects.h:22790 walks every permanent the controller has, with no type test, and GoldFishRunner's deck-trait scan stamps deck_has_mana_grant from the PARAM rather than from a card type) -- this fixture is the behavioural pin, because inspection is how the three-site presence-test hazard nearly shipped. THE BOARD IS BUILT SO THE CAST IS IMPOSSIBLE WITHOUT THE GRANT: one Forest and three Thallid Shell-Dwellers, against Spore Swarm at {3}{G} = 4 mana. Lands alone give 1 on turn 4 and 2 on turn 5, so a dead grant means Spore Swarm is NEVER castable in this fixture. With the grant, the three Shell-Dwellers each tap for {G} (they are Fungi, and DEFENDER restricts only ATTACKING -- CR 302.6 gates {T} abilities on summoning sickness, not on defender), so turn 4 has exactly 1 + 3 = 4. DAMAGE LEDGER: Spore Swarm resolves turn 4 into three 1/1 Saprolings; nothing on this board lords them and there is no Doubling Season out, so they stay 1/1. They are summoning-sick on turn 4 and the Shell-Dwellers cannot attack at all, so turn 4 deals ZERO. On turn 5 the three Saprolings attack for 3: 40 -> 37. The Shell-Dwellers' spore counters provably do not interfere -- they tick once at each of the two upkeeps and need THREE to make anything. SO THE FIXTURE DISCRIMINATES 37 (grant live) FROM 40 (grant dead), with no intermediate value available, which is what makes it a pin rather than a smoke test.
